chunks: As for what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh and Abī al-Ḥasan, peace be upon them, who said:
Regarding a man who has intercourse with a woman and then she menstruates before performing ghusl from janābah, he said: the ghusl of janābah is obligatory upon her.

So the proper way to understand this report is one of two possibilities: one of them is that we interpret it as indicating a kind of recommendation, and the second is that it is informing about the manner of the ghusl, because the ghusl of the menstruating woman is exactly like the ghusl of janābah. So it is as though he said: what is obligatory upon her is that she perform a ghusl like the ghusl of janābah. He did not say that the ghusl of janābah itself is obligatory and that, in addition to that, the ghusl of menstruation is also binding upon her. That which clarifies what we first mentioned concerning recommendation...

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity caused by intercourse
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath associated with janābah
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْحَيْضِ: the ritual bath associated with menstruation

ai.seo_question: If a woman becomes menstruating before doing ghusl from janābah, does she need one ghusl or two?
ai.summary: This report addresses the case of a woman who becomes menstruating before performing ghusl after janābah. The discussion explains that the wording may either indicate recommendation or refer to the manner of ghusl, clarifying that one ghusl suffices rather than requiring both ghusl al-janābah and ghusl al-ḥayḍ separately.
